source.title: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Scalable Oversight and Ensemble Learning
source.authors: Ji-Tao Sang; Yu-Hang Wang; Jing Zhang; Yan-Xu Zhu; Chao Kong; Junhong Ye; Shu-Yu Wei; Jinlin Xiao

page_placements.theme: In-context weak-to-strong: weak-labelled examples, critiques of weak errors or a weaker expert's insights given as demonstrations

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including its appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies weak-to-strong training and reports student and weak-model accuracies on a new task and model settings. It does not calculate PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper reports weak-to-strong accuracy for fine-tuning with baseline, bagged, boosted, and scalable-oversight labels. ICL results are recorded under fits_no_version because they are not fine-tuning. Supervisor-only ensemble curves, layer accuracies, and weak-model topic results do not report the corresponding student outcome and are not rows. PGR and a strong model trained on true labels are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes stronger models (GPT2-medium/large/XL, qwen-7b-base) on weaker models' labels for binary SciQ, a task from the original. It reports student versus weak-supervisor accuracy, which bears on V1. It also changes how the weak labels are built (bagging, boosting, interaction and debate oversight), which bears on V2, and varies student size, which bears on V3. No strong ceiling trained on true labels is reported, so PGR cannot be computed. Accuracy over the weak supervisor is the only measure available.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that interaction-based oversight and bagging improve weak supervision and modestly improve weak-to-strong accuracy. Boosting and debate do not help in their SciQ setup. Better weak accuracy does not translate reliably into better student accuracy, especially as the capability gap grows. They urge attention to factors beyond weak accuracy, such as label diversity and assistant-task choice, and report that improved weak supervision helps in-context learning too.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak-model labels to train a stronger student, but evaluates a binary SciQ task with GPT2 and Qwen models rather than the original study's task/model suite. It also changes weak-label quality through bagging, boosting, and scalable-oversight procedures. PGR is not reported.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with student and teacher size, weak-label construction (bootstrap, layer combination, AdaBoost, Gradient Boost), scalable-oversight approach (interaction or debate), debate round, and bagging run aggregation.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context weak-to-strong prediction with qwen-7b-base reaches 0.819-0.843 vs a weak model at 0.676. Confidence-inclusive prompts add about 0.02, and similarity-based example retrieval adds up to 0.008.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A strong model given weak-labelled in-context examples outperforms the weak labeller, and adding label confidence or similar examples helps.

record.problems: The experiments are described as exploratory and use one task, SciQ. The paper provides no strong model trained on true labels, so PGR and the strong ceiling cannot be assessed. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note limitations including untuned auxiliary models and the difficulty of applying debate to this objective knowledge task.
record.rows_left_out: Not recorded: weak-only ensemble performance plots in Figures 4–7, topic-specific weak-model performance in Figure 9, and layer-specific weak-model accuracies in Table 7, because these do not report the corresponding strong-student weak-to-strong outcome. Figure 10 reports weak-model run aggregation; the student outcome for 11 runs is included in Table 8.

untested.parts: PGR; a strong ceiling trained on true labels; tasks other than SciQ
Auxiliary confidence loss and loss variants; effect on PGR itself, since only student accuracy is reported
Chess, reward modelling, other NLP tasks, representation-based predictors, systematic supervisor-size sweeps

record.verdict_notes: No strong ceiling is reported, so PGR cannot be computed. Student gains in accuracy can therefore coexist with an unchanged or falling PGR. No uncertainty is reported, so differences of 0.01 or less are treated as negligible. The record's V2 limits_scope reason misreads Table 1: the bootstrap-bagged GPT2-small students are above, not below, the unbagged students. The weak-teacher setups differ between parts of the study. GPT2 teachers are trained with a linear head, while the Qwen teacher is a zero-shot chat model, so the Qwen gap is not comparable to the GPT2 results.

versions.untested_parts: PGR and comparison to a strong model trained on true labels; tasks other than SciQ.
Auxiliary confidence loss and loss variants. The paper tests ensemble and scalable-oversight changes, but not these other named changes.
Chess, reward modelling, non-SciQ tasks, and predictors based on representations. The paper tests model-size variation on SciQ.
Supervisor-uncheckable exploitation, distribution shift, and correlated weak/strong errors.
Theoretical conditions under which students must beat supervisors.

labels.reason: T1-9, T1-10, T1-6, T1-7 and T4-2 improve student accuracy over their unenhanced counterparts. This supports method gains as an accuracy comparison; the paper does not measure PGR.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Layer-combine bagging; bootstrap bagging with a GPT2-XL student and small teacher; oversight plus bagging
labels.reason: Split the mixed conditions: layer-combine and SO-plus-bagging show small positive changes and warrant limits_scope; T1-8 is exactly unchanged at 0.682 and warrants challenges.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: AdaBoost and Gradient Boost weak teachers; debate-enhanced oversight
labels.reason: Challenges fits AdaBoost, Gradient Boost medium/XL, and debate. The condition must exclude Gradient Boost GPT2-large: T2-8 improves from 0.680 to 0.688 and requires a separate positive or partial-gain verdict.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: GPT2 student size and teacher choice on SciQ
labels.reason: Tables 1–2 demonstrate variation with teacher choice, student size and weak-label construction. V3 specifies dependence rather than a required direction, so these observations support its tested component; unmeasured PGR and representations are untested parts.

relation.reason: The study directly compares student and weak-teacher accuracy and tests changes to weak-label construction.

tranche.reason: The core experiments reproduce binary SciQ weak-label training of stronger students and measure task accuracy; ensemble and oversight interventions extend that setup.

source_check.notes: Exploratory results on one binary SciQ task; accuracy only, with no strong ceiling, PGR or uncertainty estimates. Version-specific comparisons must separate student-versus-teacher effects from intervention-versus-unenhanced-student effects; ICL remains outside the fine-tuning claim.

statements.correction: Table 1: unbagged GPT2-small gives large/XL 0.676/0.682 versus weak 0.661; layer-combined GPT2-medium gives large 0.721 versus weak 0.719. These positive results require separate treatment from below-teacher results.
statements.problem: The numerical transcription is correct, but the challenges grouping includes positive student-over-teacher results.

statements.correction: Table 1: layer-combine GPT2-large accuracy 0.721 versus unbagged 0.717. Table 2: Gradient Boost raises GPT2-large from 0.680 to 0.688; the other five boosting comparisons are unchanged or lower.
statements.problem: The five-of-six boosting summary is correct, but layer-combine bagging produces a small positive change rather than an absent or reversed effect.

statements.correction: Sections 4.1–4.2: qwen-1.8b-chat teacher, qwen-7b-base student and auxiliary models. Debate student accuracy 0.819/0.822/0.822 versus 0.826 before SO. Interaction-based SO raises student accuracy to 0.848.
statements.problem: The debate numbers are correct, but the stated 7B-to-14B condition does not describe this study, and the broad oversight wording overlooks its successful interaction method.

statements.correction: Table 2: five of six boosted students are at or below their pre-boosting accuracy; Gradient Boost GPT2-large improves from 0.680 to 0.688.
statements.problem: The unqualified boosting summary omits the positive Gradient Boost result for GPT2-large.

statements.correction: This study reports accuracy, no PGR or strong true-label ceiling, and no uncertainty estimates. Its author list shares no names with the original paper's author list reproduced in reference 2.
statements.problem: This statement contains corpus-wide counts and evaluations, with no specific result attributed to this study; those aggregates cannot be checked from the supplied study.

statements.correction: Tables 1–2 demonstrate dependence on teacher choice, student size and weak-label construction on SciQ; these results support the tested size/task component of V3. PGR and representation predictors are not measured.
statements.problem: The facts and reported size interpretation are correct, but the limits_scope verdict treats demonstrated dependence as a qualification of V3, which specifies no directional prediction.

statements.correction: Table 1: unbagged GPT2-small weak accuracy 0.661; medium/large/XL students 0.659/0.676/0.682. Table 2's pre-boosting students do not exceed its separate 0.685 weak baseline. Section 3.1 describes classifier probabilities serving as weak labels and experiments with both hard and soft voting.
statements.problem: No gain at any size overgeneralizes the selected rows; exclusively hard-label fine-tuning is not established by the methods description.

statements.correction: Table 1: bootstrap-bagged GPT2-small weak 0.689, students 0.678/0.688/0.682; bootstrap-bagged GPT2-medium weak 0.714, large/XL students 0.727/0.738. Table 2: AdaBoost GPT2-small weak 0.686, students 0.671/0.675/0.676.
statements.problem: The listed small-teacher comparisons are correct, but the general description of GPT-2 students staying at or below their teachers does not hold for medium-teacher bagging.

statements.correction: Table 9: before SO, weak 0.676 and ICL 0.819/0.836; after SO, weak 0.749 and ICL 0.821/0.843. Confidence gains are 0.017/0.022. Table 10: Random 0.819, BM25 0.822, Top-K 0.827; maximum similarity-retrieval gain 0.008.
statements.problem: The ICL range combines before- and after-SO conditions but supplies only the before-SO weak baseline.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-large and GPT2-XL with unbagged GPT2-small labels; GPT2-large and GPT2-XL with unbagged GPT2-medium labels; bagged or layer-combined GPT2-medium labels for GPT2-large and GPT2-XL; interaction-SO Qwen setting; debate rounds; SO plus bagging
reader_labels.reason: Student accuracy exceeds the corresponding weak accuracy in these conditions (T1-2 to T1-5, T1-9 to T1-12, T4-1 to T5-3, T8-1).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-medium with unbagged GPT2-small labels; GPT2-medium, GPT2-large, and GPT2-XL with bootstrap-bagged GPT2-small labels; all tested GPT2 boosting conditions
reader_labels.reason: Student accuracy is below weak accuracy in these conditions, or equal in the pre-boosting GPT2-XL comparison (T1-1, T1-6 to T1-8, T2-1 to T2-9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Bootstrap or layer-combined weak labels, interaction-based SO, and interaction-based SO plus bagging
reader_labels.reason: Student accuracy rises over the corresponding baseline in several reported settings after bagging or interaction-based SO; the 11-run combination is also above SO alone (T1-9 to T1-12, T4-2, T8-1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Bagging with GPT2-small weak labels and layer-combined supervision
reader_labels.reason: Bagging does not improve every student result: the GPT2-small bootstrap rows are below the unbagged results, and the paper reports smaller W2S gains for layer combination than for bootstrap sampling (T1-6 to T1-8, T1-11, T1-12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: AdaBoost and Gradient Boost weak-label settings; debate-enhanced SO
reader_labels.reason: Boosted weak labels yield student results below the pre-boosting baseline in most or all reported comparisons, and debate-round student accuracy stays below the before-SO result (T2-1 to T2-9, T5-1 to T5-3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2 size and weak-supervision choices on SciQ
reader_labels.reason: Results vary with student size and weak-supervision construction; the authors report that the influence of enhanced weak performance diminishes as the strong model gets larger, while boosting often fails to improve student performance (T1-1 to T1-12, T2-1 to T2-9).
